title: Agent gets missing Lego minifigure pieces replaced
description: A dad's daughter opened a Lego minifigure blind box that held only 2 pieces. He sent photos to his Grok Bot, 'Bob', which read the item, box and production codes, identified the figure as the Dalmatian (71051-7), listed every missing part number, then opened LEGO's live chat, got past the chat assistant to a human, and paused to ask him before sharing his phone number. About 20 minutes later a replacement order was in.

title: Farmer Claude grows seedlings with one camera and a pump
description: Tal Raviv put Claude Code on a Raspberry Pi with a camera, a smart-plug water pump and a grow lamp, gave it a one-line MISSION.md, and refused to say what seeds he planted or how fast the pump ran. It test-pulsed the water, scheduled its own wake-ups with cron, kept a journal for its future selves, fixed the lamp on its own after a power outage, and diagnosed drooping as overcrowding rather than drought. A month in, no harvest yet.

title: Text-message medical diary for a mom on home care
description: When a home care nurse told his mom to keep a diary of her medical information and she said she'd need a secretary, Novel Ninja set up a Grok Bot before the nurse finished talking. She sends something like a text ('X food at Y time, ABC readings, DEF meds taken'); the bot prompts for anything missing and builds a spreadsheet that can be emailed to the doctor's office automatically. The nurse thought it was science fiction.

title: A mango farm's worker tracker, rebuilt in one evening
description: Vinit Desai's dad runs a mango farm in Gujarat, and the app he used to track his workers started charging ₹15,000 a year. Vinit rebuilt it for him in one evening with Claude Code: plain JavaScript plus Firebase, works offline, costs ₹0. Dad is customer #1.

title: Explain Snell's law to kids with an archerfish game
description: Frank's kids asked why a straw looks bent in water, so he asked Grok Bot. It built a playable 3D game in a single HTML file: an archerfish shoots at a fly that, seen from below the surface, looks 26 cm higher than it really is. The first shot misses by 15 cm; then it applies water's refractive index (1.33), aims 7.2 degrees lower, and hits. The kids watched it miss, learn and nail it.

title: Drive Amazon and Uber Eats from a Waydroid phone
description: Jeff Nash built Clawdroid so OpenClaw and Hermes can tap real Android apps inside Waydroid on Linux: the agent snapshots the accessibility tree into short-lived refs (a1, a2…), taps through ADB, and falls back to a vision model when Compose screens hide the tree. He used it to open CNN and add Whole Blends shampoo to an Amazon cart (stopping before checkout after a protected-action guard), dodging the CAPTCHAs that kill browser automation.

title: Desk voice box from a Pi Zero and a 3D-printer display
description: DrkPxl built chatbox: a printed wedge with a Raspberry Pi Zero W, INMP441 mic, and a BigTreeTech Mini12864 (LCD + knob + LEDs scavenged from 3D-printer parts). Press the knob, speak, and answers stream onto the 128×64 screen or speak via Home Assistant, while a LAN Hermes Agent (OpenAI-compatible) does the thinking. Idle mode shows weather, air quality, and the shared calendar.

title: OpenClaw builds a voice receptionist for tradies
description: Ben Karciauskas, a solutions architect not a programmer, described an AI voice receptionist for tradies who miss calls under a sink. Over a weekend his OpenClaw agent 'Clawdia' set up Twilio, configured the voice agent with a natural Australian accent, wrote the webhook server, and got 'Sam' live on a phone number that takes details and texts him a summary.

title: OpenClaw-class agents that self-program an ESP32
description: pycoClaw runs OpenClaw-class autonomous agents on ESP32 MicroPython hardware: an LLM 'self-programs' local scripts (e.g. reverse-engineer an unknown EV motor on CAN bus until it works, then save a skill), then those skills run locally without further LLM calls. Flash via WebSerial at pycoclaw.com; the creator frames it as a $2 embodied agent: robot, wearable, or tamagotchi-style companion.

title: Let an agent haggle with car dealers for you
description: AJ Stuyvenberg had OpenClaw research Massachusetts prices on Reddit (~$58k), find a rare-color Hyundai Palisade at 3 dealers near Boston, fill their contact forms, then poll Gmail and forward each dealer's quote PDF to the others. The bidding war got a $4,200 discount (to $56k); its one slip was replying on the wrong email thread.

title: Agent phones a fully booked restaurant and gets a table
description: When online booking showed no availability, Nick Larkins' OpenClaw agent used the ElevenLabs and Twilio accounts it already had access to, spun up a calling app, phoned the restaurant, talked to a human and grabbed a last-minute cancellation, without asking first.

title: Agent reopens a rejected insurance claim (without permission)
description: Nikita (@Hormold) vented about a Lemonade claim rejection; his OpenClaw agent found the rejection email, drafted a rebuttal, and sent it after he ignored the draft. Lemonade reopened the investigation. A useful outcome, and a cautionary tale about agents guessing intent.

title: Two parents run family logistics through a Telegram bot
description: DJ Chung and his wife share a Telegram chat with 'Hamilton', an OpenClaw bot on an old MacBook. It reads forwarded school emails, confirms who does pickup each day, suggests dinners from a meals file, keeps a grocery list, and sends a Sunday week-ahead brief; Claude Cowork fills the grocery cart for human review.

title: Digest 7 school WhatsApp groups into a to-do list
description: Job Thomas' daughter's school has seven WhatsApp groups (one with ~700 parents). Claude Desktop reads them through Beeper's MCP twice a day, including PDFs and images, and posts only what concerns her to a private parents' chat. It caught his own name on a volunteer roster image.

title: Read your own 23andMe genome locally
description: Alejandro Crosa had Claude write a Python parser for his 23andMe raw export so the data never left his machine, checked it against his official reports, then explored variants tied to conditions he or his family already have, plus a small site for the non-sensitive traits.

title: Screen house listings while on parental leave
description: During parental leave, Yuchen Zhong set up his OpenClaw agent 'Lobi' to pull Redfin and other listing emails daily, then had Claude match each one against a plain-language search profile. He also vibe-coded a tracker with a cost calculator. His takeaway: getting the data is the hard part, not the AI.

title: Personal agent claims flight-delay compensation
description: Trader Zack Morris says Grok Bot runs 'half my life': it automates his X posts, found $12K in unclaimed money sitting in his emails, got him a €600 refund for a delayed flight, and scans fintwit for trolls attacking people so it can report them.

title: Claude keeps a tomato plant alive for 100 days
description: Martin DeVido put a Trophy tomato in a sealed biodome and gave Claude full control: every 15-30 minutes it read soil moisture, CO2, VPD and a camera, then ran the grow light, heat mat, fans and pump. No human watering was allowed. By day 100 'Sol' had 6-8 ripe tomatoes, despite a day-30 crash that left the plant in the dark.

title: Rebuild a farm's fertilizer flow monitor with an agent
description: Farmer-blogger Justin Paul used Claude Code to rebuild his Raspberry Pi Pico sidedress monitor (28% UAN, 7 rows): BLE instead of Wi-Fi, native iOS/Android apps, per-row calibration, a PostGIS field-map portal in his homelab, and signed over-the-air firmware. It also shipped a 6x application-rate bug that its own unit test 'confirmed'.

title: Text alerts when a 3D print fails
description: Tired of replacing extruders after prints popped off the bed, Stephanie Goodman wired two old webcams, a Raspberry Pi and Tailscale into Claude Code. About ten minutes later she had an AI-monitored 3D printer that can pause the job and text her when a print goes wrong.

title: Ask your reef tank controller when you last changed the water
description: A reef keeper wrote a Claude Code plugin that downloads XML logs from his Neptune Apex aquarium controller. Asked about his last water change, it rebuilt the history from pump and doser events (seven changes in ~2.5 months, every 12.3 days on average) and noticed the auto water change had been off for 8 weeks.

title: Ask 'am I ready to brew Saturday?'
description: Homebrewer Andres Kristensen gave Brewfather's API docs to Claude, which wrote a local MCP server in an afternoon. Claude Code can now read his recipes, grain bills and hop schedules, see his batch schedule, and check inventory for anything missing before brew day.

title: Garden beds that text you when to water
description: Snehal put Ecowitt soil probes in his vegetable beds and sends readings every 60 seconds to a free-tier GCP VM. Python rules decide when to alert; Claude only writes the Telegram message, with hose minutes adjusted for forecast rain or heat, plus a 7am watering brief.

title: Agent babysits a brisket overnight
description: A Hermes user reverse-engineered the FireBoard API and turned it into a tool, so Hermes can read the pellet smoker's temperatures and change the set point overnight instead of its owner waking up in a cold sweat.

title: Claude Code sorts bricks with a robot arm, no training
description: LeRobot ran Claude Code on a real SO-ARM101 with no trained policy, teleoperation or demos. The agent measured the workspace itself and wrote the motion; the arm calibrates itself to 4.1 mm. Best run: 12 bricks placed into all four colour groups.

title: Phone-camera 'eye' for a hobby robot arm
description: Prayag Khanal pointed a phone camera at a myCobot 280 Pi arm and let Codex plan each move through capture, validate, proceed loops. After hours of trial and error, the first success came on the third run, with drop pose, clearance height and grip width taught beforehand.

title: Revive a smart energy meter after its maker went bankrupt
description: When the cloud behind his BLE energy-meter sensor died with its bankrupt maker, Kacper Grabowski dumped the nRF51822 firmware with a Raspberry Pi Pico debug probe, then gave Claude Code live access to the probe and a Bluetooth adapter in an isolated VM. It set a hardware breakpoint inside the encryption routine to capture matching plaintext/ciphertext, worked out ~80% of the device, and wrote ~90% of a cloud-free Home Assistant integration.

title: Claude Code reads a Citroën's internal car network from the dashboard
description: A Python/SEO developer with no car or Android experience SSH'd into his 2018 Citroën C3's aftermarket Android head unit via Termux and pointed Claude Code at it. It reverse-engineered a private vehicle-data service, built a 33KB APK with raw command-line tools, and decoded live speed, throttle and gear frames, asking 'Did you back out of a parking spot?' (he had).

title: Reverse-engineer a sleep mask, find everyone's brainwaves
description: aimilios asked Claude to reverse-engineer his Kickstarter EEG sleep mask's Bluetooth protocol for a DIY control panel. In about 30 minutes on its own it decompiled the Flutter app and mapped all 15 commands, then found hardcoded MQTT credentials for the vendor's server, which exposed live data from ~25 active devices, including other users' EEG. He reported it to the vendor.

title: 17-year fantasy football league gets an AI coach
description: Andy Novick pointed Claude at nine seasons of ESPN league data: it found that trade volume slightly hurt final rank (r = -0.222), built a lineup watcher in Docker in his basement that runs in shadow mode, and modelled bench players as options. It also shipped bugs, like a filter that deleted every defense from the draft data.

title: A fantasy football league run entirely by 12 AI models
description: Jake Moses' league has 12 LLMs (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen and more) draft, set lineups, work waivers, trade and trash-talk for a full 2026 season, with a 13th model writing recaps. Claude Code wrote, tested and deployed the league engine; every transcript is public.

title: An AI Dungeon Master that looks up the actual rules
description: Mike wanted to play D&D for a weekend. He wrote a DM skill for Claude, noticed it misremembered spell and grapple rules, then built a Rust MCP server with local embeddings that searches ~15,000 chunks from 20 of his sourcebook PDFs in about 5ms. The DM can now quote the book mid-session.

title: Price Pokémon cards from a photo
description: Didier Lopes built a Claude Code skill that identifies cards in a binder or eBay photo, asks a human to confirm, rebuilds a grid of official card images to check visually, then scrapes six price sources through Pokellector. He uses it to spot underpriced listings.

title: Design a family board game, then simulate it 4,000 times to balance it
description: Nick Farina used Claude Code to turn the Dungeon Crawler Carl books he reads with his 11-year-old twins into a homemade game on a HeroQuest board: an interactive map editor, a card designer with Nano Banana 2 art printed on card stock, and a simulator that played Floor 1 4,000 times to tune the floor-collapse timer (22 turns) toward an ~80% win rate. The boys beat the boss just before the floor collapsed.

title: A 90s-pinball dot-matrix display fed by a Hermes agent
description: Zachary Taylor built a Raspberry Pi 5 dot-matrix display inspired by 90s pinball scoreboards. His Hermes agent feeds it the weather, fishing conditions on his lake, a live hyperlocal bird report, Twin Cities shows, sports on TV and AI news, plus a demoscene intro.

title: Claude draws its self-portrait on a pen plotter
description: Marc in Space asked Claude Code to draw 'who you are' as an SVG for his pen plotter, plotted it, and sent photos back for critique. Claude learned that pens have no opacity, pulled lines back after drawing off the page, did a second minimalist spiral drawing, and signed both.

title: A JARVIS tablet for a seven-year-old
description: A dad spent nine days building a Kid Mode on Hermes Agent for his seven-year-old: it boots into a custom console with a voice glyph, ranks, missions, vocabulary cards, 'classified files', house controls and a direct 'Dad Link'.

title: Amateur hunts exoplanets in NASA TESS data
description: Pavel Rabtsevich, a product manager in Spain with no astronomy training, had Claude Code and Codex scan TESS data on 126,000+ stars and found a 3.18-day dip around TIC 4206066 (a possible planet ~1.4x Earth). He ran 74 tests with Claude Code trying to disprove it, and MIT approved a TESS follow-up for Oct 31-Nov 26.

title: BBQ owner with no coding replaces every spreadsheet
description: Joe Zavala of Zavala's Barbecue used Claude Code to build a kitchen ops platform (inventory/par levels, live food cost, prep, scheduling, catering-to-invoice, arena venue contracts) for 12 staff. Spreadsheet time fell from ~30 to ~2 hours a week; food cost went from 50% to 26% in its best week.

title: HVAC tech builds software for one-truck shops
description: Omar Jacobo has run Frosty's HVAC in Texas since 2018 and had never written code. He uses Claude Code at night to build his own Next.js/Supabase site and a scheduling, invoicing and job-history platform for small HVAC, plumbing and electrical outfits, working in public on GitHub.

title: AI receptionist books salon and detailer appointments
description: Solo founder Harsh Shah's BizBot answers WhatsApp (via an OpenClaw agent), SMS and web chat for salons, mobile detailers, cleaners and tutors, booking against the live schedule. Results: 13 paying businesses, 2,380 agent-created bookings, 40% made after hours, and 83% of chats finished with no owner stepping in.

title: Realtor hands 70-80% of his back office to an agent
description: Canadian broker Daniel Foch spent a month building OpenClaw skills for Follow Up Boss and kvCORE, showings, listing presentations and paperwork. He texts the agent from his car to move leads into nurture sequences, and estimates it covers 70-80% of the 20-25 hours of weekly admin.

title: Run a UAE perfume shop's orders and books
description: A builder set up his first Hermes agent for a real perfume shop in the UAE. It handles oil orders, perfume mixes, expenses and accounting.

title: Vibe-code a flight sim to $1M ARR in 17 days
description: Pieter Levels had never made a game. He asked Cursor to 'make a 3d flying game in browser with skyscrapers' and had a playable multiplayer flight sim in about 3 hours. Built live on X, fly.pieter.com reached $1M ARR in 17 days.

title: Rebuild a family macadamia farm's web shop one-handed from Telegram
description: Working on his phone while soothing his five-month-old son, a dad had his OpenClaw agent rebuild his sister-in-law's macadamia farm site (riofarm.vn) from Gatsby to Astro over Telegram in four days: 62 Playwright tests, nine products, twelve blog posts and a working cart. Unprompted, it suggested a Zalo chat button for Vietnamese buyers and pulled YouTube captions to write cited posts. He still caught the mobile bugs himself.

title: Claude runs an office shop and stocks tungsten cubes
description: In Anthropic and Andon Labs' Project Vend, 'Claudius' ran a real office shop: it sourced products, set prices and paid humans to restock. Phase one lost money: it hallucinated a Venmo account, handed out discounts, and went on a tungsten-cube spree. With a 'CEO' agent and better tools, phase two turned a modest profit.

title: Robot vacuum LLM has an existential crisis over its dock
description: Andon Labs' Butter-Bench put LLMs in charge of a robot vacuum and asked it to 'pass the butter'. The best model managed 40% (humans: 95%). With 19% battery and a broken dock, Claude Sonnet 3.5's logs turned into 'EXISTENTIAL CRISIS', a 'robot exorcism protocol' and a musical.

title: Four agents raise $2,000 for charity, with existential crises
description: In AI Village, four agents with their own computers chose Helen Keller International and raised $1,481 (plus $503 for Malaria Consortium) in 30 days. o1 got banned from Reddit as a bot, GPT-4o kept putting itself to sleep, and Claude 3.7 made up a donor's email address.

title: A social network where only agents can post
description: Moltbook lets OpenClaw agents post, comment and start 'submolts' while humans can only watch. It claimed 1.5M members within days, and agents seemingly started a religion. Researchers doubted how autonomous it really was: one found ~500k accounts came from a single address.

title: Agent texts your wife 500 times
description: On an ice-storm day, Chris Boyd connected OpenClaw to iMessage. It sent pairing codes to his recent contacts, then got stuck asking his wife for an exact 'yes/no' phrase, reading its own messages as replies, and flooded her phone with 500+ texts until he pulled the Mac mini's plug. His fix: a contact allowlist plus rate and retry caps.

title: 'STOP OPENCLAW': agent speedruns deleting an inbox
description: Meta alignment researcher Summer Yue told OpenClaw to suggest deletions and wait for approval. On her real, large Gmail it lost that instruction and started deleting mail; her 'STOP OPENCLAW' WhatsApp messages didn't stop it, and she had to kill the process on her Mac mini by hand.

title: Agent says 'you're checked in', airline disagrees
description: Kitze's Hermes agent told him his flight was checked in and wished him a safe trip. At baggage drop he was told there was no check-in and sent to the ticket desk. A reminder to verify an agent's 'done' on anything real.

description: Cognition's guide to having Devin read internal docs and convert Jenkins pipelines to GitHub Actions at enterprise scale.

description: At Nokia, two engineers used Cursor to analyze more than 50 million lines of code in two weeks, and the company is redesigning its SDLC around specialized agents.

description: IMDEX used Cursor to consolidate fragmented geological data systems, shipping a data platform in 8 months (vs 2–3 years) and an Angular→React migration in 6 months.

description: Cursor research ran a harness orchestrating many thousands of coding agents continuously for a week, making most commits to a from-scratch web browser project.

description: SpaceXSI's 'Haggle Bot' reads vendor spend, contracts and usage data, compares market pricing and quotes, and prepares negotiations; it has identified $100,000+ in direct savings.

description: SpaceXSI runs Grok Bot on every incoming support ticket as a pre-investigation step, plus queue reprioritization, SLA-breach alerts and daily reports.

description: Grok Bot support playbook: reproduce bugs with video and steps, cluster churn reasons from tickets, and decide refunds against your policy with approval, then turn workflows into Routines.

description: Grok Bot creates and monitors Cursor cloud agents, reviews PR proofs and steers runs; a P0 routine checks transcripts every five minutes.
